directions.description: Test a larger causal receptive field and bottleneck residual blocks within NextItNet. The original NextItNet paper and author implementation provide the architectural reference: [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.05163), [code](https://github.com/fajieyuan/WSDM2019-nextitnet). Improvement on this benchmark remains a hypothesis.
directions.implementation: Start from the supplied corrected NextItNet. Test dilations [1,2,4,8,16,32,64,1] with eight residual blocks, kernel size 3, hidden size 64 and maxlen 128. Compare against the baseline dilation cycle before changing width. A subsequent architecture variant can use the author's bottleneck residual design with pointwise reduction, causal dilated convolution and pointwise expansion. Mask padding after every residual block and after final normalization. Preserve shifted causal targets and final-nonpadding readout. Expose log2feats(sequence) as encode_sequence(sequence), retain item_emb, and implement predict_score(features, items) using the same embedding-dot-product scoring as forward and score_candidates. Save architecture parameters in category metadata and update the predictor writer to reconstruct them exactly. Shared requirements for all four directions: DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; retain all four categories and routing; preprocessing seed 0 and training seed 42; exactly 200 batches per epoch and at most 200 epochs; single-GPU execution; trial-local artifacts; one independently trained checkpoint per category. Keep supplied splits and host evaluation unchanged, select using macro validation HR@10, and perform no score fusion, checkpoint averaging or external-weight loading.

directions.description: Replace one-negative BPR with multiple-negative gBCE while retaining the NextItNet encoder. This transfers only the training objective from [gSASRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.07192) and its [official PyTorch implementation](https://github.com/asash/gSASRec-pytorch); it does not adopt the SASRec backbone.
directions.implementation: Preserve sample_batch's causal seq/pos contract and its returned negative array for diagnosis compatibility. Inside the loss, sample K training-only negatives per valid position, excluding padding, the target and that user's training interactions. Start with K=64 and calibration t=0.5; consider K=128 and t=0.75 only if budget permits. With alpha=K/(itemnum-1), beta=1-t+alpha*t, positive log-probability a=beta*torch.nn.functional.logsigmoid(s_pos.double()), compute positive loss as -a-log(-torch.expm1(a)); compute negative loss as torch.nn.functional.softplus(s_neg.double()). Sum the positive term and K negative terms, divide by K+1, and average over pos!=0. This stable expression implements -log(1-sigmoid(s_pos)^beta). Keep raw embedding-dot-product scores at inference. Allow sufficient early-stopping patience for calibrated-loss warm-up, within the 200-epoch cap. No inference architecture change is required; keep the predictor writer and checkpoint class identical.

directions.description: Use BPR-max to emphasize difficult negatives instead of comparing each target with one uniformly sampled item. Borrow the objective from the authors' [top-k gains paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03847) and [official PyTorch code](https://github.com/hidasib/GRU4Rec_PyTorch_Official), retaining NextItNet throughout.
directions.implementation: Leave the corrected NextItNet architecture and causal training pairs unchanged. Generate K=64 eligible uniform negatives per nonpadding target using training interactions only. For positive score p and negative scores n, compute log_w=torch.log_softmax(n,dim=-1), ranking_loss=-torch.logsumexp(log_w+torch.nn.functional.logsigmoid(p.unsqueeze(-1)-n),dim=-1), and score_regularizer=(log_w.exp()*n.square()).sum(-1). Optimize mean(ranking_loss+lambda*score_regularizer) over valid positions, initially lambda=0.01; test 0.001 or 0.1 only as separate budgeted trials. Preserve the family-specific sampler interface by adding extra negatives inside the loss or through an optional helper. Candidate inference remains the same single NextItNet dot-product scorer, so no additional predictor or fitted popularity component is introduced.

directions.description: Add dropout-view contrastive regularization to the same NextItNet network. Adapt the shared-encoder consistency idea from [DuoRec's paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.05730) and [author implementation](https://github.com/RuihongQiu/DuoRec/blob/master/recbole/model/sequential_recommender/duorec.py), without adopting its Transformer.
directions.implementation: Keep baseline BPR initially to isolate the regularizer. Encode each sampled sequence twice through the exact same NextItNet parameters with independent dropout masks. Gather each view at the maximum position where seq!=0, normalize its feature vector, and form a symmetric InfoNCE loss over the 2B vectors with temperature 0.2. Exclude self-similarities; the paired dropout view is the positive. Mask other rows sharing the same final training target so they are not treated as negatives. Add 0.05*contrastive_loss to the sequence BPR loss; consider coefficients 0.01 and 0.1 in subsequent trials. Both views must contain only the supplied causal inputs, never their shifted targets. Use one optimizer and one checkpoint per category. At inference run the network once with dropout disabled, preserving the existing scorer and predictor writer; there is no second encoder, momentum teacher or averaging.
